name: ITM2B Amyloidosis
aliases: Familial British and Danish Dementia Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic mutation in ITM2B gene
Histological evidence of amyloid deposits in affected tissues
Presence of progressive cognitive decline and/or sensorineural hearing loss

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic ITM2B mutation plus histological confirmation of amyloid deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing and tissue biopsy demonstrating amyloid deposits; clinical features support diagnosis.

laboratory: Detection of amyloid fibrils by Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid tau and amyloid-beta abnormalities
imaging: MRI showing cerebral amyloid angiopathy and white matter changes
Brain PET scan demonstrating amyloid deposition
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in ITM2B gene (e.g., British and Danish dementia mutations)
other: Histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits in brain or affected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: More common age of onset and clinical progression

redFlags: Early onset progressive dementia with family history
Sensorineural hearing loss combined with cognitive decline
Histological evidence of amyloid deposits in brain or peripheral tissues
references: Campion D, et al. Familial British dementia: a novel form of hereditary cerebral amyloidosis. Brain. 1999.
Ghiso J, et al. Familial Danish dementia: clinical, neuropathological, and biochemical studies. Ann Neurol. 2001.
